result:
REST, unless you already know your consumers need highly variable, deeply nested reads.

HTTP caching, CDNs, rate limiting and per-endpoint auth work out of the box with REST, whereas GraphQL makes you build query-cost analysis and depth limiting to stop a single expensive query from hurting you. Every third-party developer already knows REST and can hit it with curl, so onboarding and support costs are lower for a public audience you don't control. An OpenAPI spec gives you generated SDKs, docs and contract tests for free, and versioning or deprecating endpoints is easier to observe and enforce than tracking field usage across arbitrary queries.

GraphQL is the better pick if your main consumers are rich front-ends or mobile apps that stitch many related resources per screen, since it removes over-fetching and round trips; in that case you can still add it later on top of the same service layer.
